hens_rule_text: Fowl are capped at roughly 20 per acre, which works out to about 5 chickens on a typical quarter-acre lot; a paid annual permit and property inspection are required regardless of flock size.
permit_notes: An annual permit from Charlotte-Mecklenburg Animal Care & Control is required, with a reported $40 fee and a pre-issuance inspection.
setback_notes: Coop must be at least 25 ft from any property line; no distance specifically from neighboring homes was found.
coop_rules: Coop must be fully enclosed, well ventilated, cleaned daily, and provide at least 4 sq ft of floor area per bird; fowl must be confined at all times.
zoning_notes: Rules are in Charlotte Municipal Code Sec. 3-102, applying citywide to equine, cloven-hoofed animals and domestic fowl, contingent on a city permit application. Roosters are not explicitly banned but a permit can be denied over expected noise nuisance.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: American Farmland Trust, Charlotte North Carolina Urban Livestock Ordinance

research_notes: The Municipal Code text of Sec. 3-102 was not directly opened (Municode region block, no Wayback copy found); the 20-per-acre density figure, $40 fee and 25 ft setback come from secondary summaries and a farmland-law database citing the 2010 ordinance, not the current code text, so exact current numbers are unconfirmed.
